rows.text:
Ines Okafor, the new Keeper of the Salt Ledger, works on Harrow Quay, where Mara Venn is the harbourmaster and Aldous Brandt was the former keeper. Ines Okafor was sent to take up the post of Keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay.

Mara Venn showed Ines Okafor the Salt Ledger, which she needs audited before the equinox market, and Ines found the spring pages torn out.

Mara Venn left Ines Okafor alone in the archive with the lamp, after saying that some believe Aldous Brandt took the torn pages with him. Who tore the spring pages out of the Salt Ledger, and why, before Aldous Brandt disappeared from Harrow Quay?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor is the new Keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay, taking over from Aldous Brandt, who kept the book for thirty years. Anselm Pike is the island's physician and printer, who offered to help Ines Okafor with the book. Ines Okafor was asked by the council, through Mara Venn, to finish the audit of the Salt Ledger before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren denied carrying Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left. Ines Okafor found the spring pages of the Salt Ledger torn out, and Mara Venn said the book was found that way. Mara Lisle said Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping in his last month and went to the salt warehouse at night. An unsigned note pushed under the archive door claimed the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it away. Ines Okafor counted the salt over four days and found twenty-four barrels a month had never reached the ledger.

Ines Okafor dropped a printed handbill pasted over the November page into the stove and went on working. What was Aldous Brandt counting in the salt warehouse, and why did he never tell Mara Lisle?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new Keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt kept the Salt Ledger for thirty years before leaving the island, and he had been gone for three weeks. Ines Okafor was asked by the council, through Mara Venn, to finish the audit of the Salt Ledger before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren gave Ines Okafor a small brass key that Aldous Brandt had given him, and told her to keep it off the ledger. Ines Okafor found the spring pages of the Salt Ledger torn out, and Mara Venn said the book was found that way. Mara Lisle said that in his last month Aldous Brandt went to the salt warehouse at night and came back with chalk on his sleeves. An unsigned note was pushed under the archive door, claiming the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk. Ines Okafor found that twenty-four barrels of salt a month had reached the island without ever being recorded in the ledger. Ines Okafor found a printed handbill pasted over the margin of the November page of the ledger.

Ines Okafor peeled the handbill off with a knife, dropped it in the stove, and went back to her counting. Who has been moving the unrecorded salt onto the island, and who is buying the fish it cures?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt was the Salt Ledger's former keeper for thirty years and had been gone three weeks. Ines Okafor was asked by the council, through Mara Venn, to finish the audit before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren insisted he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account. Ines Okafor found the Salt Ledger's spring pages torn out, which Mara Venn said were already missing when Brandt left. Mara Lisle said Aldous Brandt went to the salt warehouse at night with a lantern in his last month. Ines Okafor counted salt over four days and found twenty-four barrels a month arriving unrecorded in the ledger. Mara Venn refused to open the sealed salt warehouse without a council order. Someone took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the desk in the archive after the lamp had gone out.

Anselm Pike offered to keep the receipts in a strongbox in his dispensary, saying nobody searches a doctor. Who stood beside Ines Okafor in the dark, and why did they take only her salt tally sheet?

rows.text:
Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry. Aldous Brandt was the former keeper of the Salt Ledger for thirty years, and had been gone for three weeks. Mara Venn was the harbourmaster, who led Ines Okafor to the archive and passed on the council's request. Ines Okafor was asked by the council, through Mara Venn, to finish the Salt Ledger audit before the equinox market.

Tobiah Wren said he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left. Tobiah Wren left Ines Okafor on the quay and sailed north to the cod banks, not returning before the equinox. Ines Okafor found the spring pages of the Salt Ledger torn out, and Mara Venn said the book had been found that way the morning Brandt was gone. Anselm Pike brought Ines Okafor soup and told her he had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years. Mara Lisle said that in his last month Aldous Brandt went to the salt warehouse at night with a lantern. An unsigned note pushed under the archive door said the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk. Ines Okafor counted salt over four days and found twenty-four barrels a month arriving on the island without reaching the ledger. Mara Venn refused to open the salt warehouse without a council order, saying it was sealed until the market. That night a second note signed by the Cormorant was pushed under the archive door. An unseen visitor took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the desk, while the ledger and receipts were left untouched.

Anselm Pike found Ines Okafor on the tower steps at first light and was all concern. Anselm Pike offered to hide the receipts tin in his dispensary strongbox, saying nobody searches a doctor. Who stood beside Ines Okafor in the dark and took her salt tally sheet from the archive desk?
